newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bishop calls for economic change.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bishop calls for economic change.

text.p: An Argentine bishop on Saturday attacked government plans to reform the labour market and said what was really necessary to alleviate the country's suffering was the creation of jobs.
In a tough criticism of the government's spending cuts the Bishop of Quilmes, Jorge Novak, in a homily read at mass said "God does not agree with the pain caused by unnatural and unjust policies."
He called for a change in the government's economic policies and asked for relief for the country's unemployed and destitute.

Argentina's government has recently reduced family benefits and introduced taxes on shopping vouchers received by many workers as a large part of their pay packets, biting hard into the pockets of many Argentines.

Trade unions have staged two general strikes in recent months protesting the government's policies that has left 17.1 percent of the workforce without jobs. The Church has joined unions and opposition parties in criticising the government.

At the mass in a suburb of Buenos Aires, Novak said "it is not the will of God that our children grow up with malnutrition, that our young see their horizons without happiness and creativity, that our pensioners lead a languid existence, nearly like a prolonged agony."
